So relation maybe "primary agricultural product". Subject Tennessee, object each product. Also "major manufacturing exports include chemicals, transportation equipment, electrical equipment". So relation "major manufacturing export". Then Great Smoky Mountains National Park is "headquartered in the eastern part of the state". So subject "Great Smoky Mountains National Park", relation "headquartered in", object "eastern part of Tennessee". Could also be location "eastern Tennessee". We'll treat object as "eastern Tennessee". Also "nation's most visited national park". That's a qualifier: "superlative" maybe "most visited". Could add qualifier "superlative" but not required. We'll maybe add qualifier "ranking" but not needed. We'll just capture "most visited national park" as a qualifier? The rule: qualifiers must be attached. So we could have relation "rank" with object "most visited". But maybe better: relation "description" with object "nation's most visited national park". But we need short unambiguous relation. Could use "most visited" as qualifier of "national park". Might skip.

Next: "a section of the Appalachian Trail roughly follows the Tennessee-North Carolina border." So subject "Appalachian Trail", relation "follows", object "Tennessee-North Carolina border". Qualifier "approximation" maybe "roughly". So add qualifier "approximation" with object "roughly". Also "section of the Appalachian Trail" but we treat subject as "Appalachian Trail".
